items.title: Being a monomorphism is fpqc local on the base (two proofs: diagonal descent and reduction to schemes)
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The author gives two complete, independent arguments. First proof: f is a monomorphism iff its diagonal \Delta is an isomorphism; each base-changed diagonal \Delta_i is an isomorphism and is the base change of \Delta; the fpqc covering pulls back to an fpqc covering of X \times_Y X; descent of the isomorphism property (cited) makes \Delta an isomorphism. Second proof: reduce to Y a scheme via a surjective \'etale chart, using a sheaf-theoretic injectivity lemma for the cartesian square with c surjective; refine the covering so the Y_i are schemes too; then for a, b : T \to X with f \circ a = f \circ b, the base changes agree (f_i monomorphism) over the fpqc covering {Y_i \times_Y T \to T}, and the fpqc sheaf proposition (cited) gives a = b. Two full arguments with a sheaf-level lemma inside are the substance.
